newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end lower, following soybeans.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end lower, following soybeans.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures ended lower on Wednesday, taking cues from soybeans, with new-crop hit by forecasts for much-needed rains in portions of the U.S. Midwest, traders said.
Meteorologists said two rain systems were forecast to move across the U.S. Midwest thorugh early next week, with the second system offering the best chance of rain for dry areas in central Illinois.
Traders said soymeal drew some pressure from news Tyson Foods Inc had temporarily suspended poultry slaughter at an Arkansas plant due to concern over dioxin levels.

Soy products were also weakened by the National Oilseed Processors Association monthly crush data. NOPA on Wednesday put June soyoil stocks at roughly 1.746 billion lbs, down from 1.750 in last month's report.

"The decline in soyoil stocks I thought was a bit of a surprise," said Ann Frick, analyst with Prudential Securities. "I had thought we'd see more of a decline because we had such a pickup in exports recently."
Soymeal ended $7.50 to $5.60 per ton lower with August off $7.50 at $244.40. Soyoil closed down 0.55 to 0.30 cent per lb with August down 0.53 at 22.26.

On the day, Continental Grain sold 400 lots August soymeal and 200 July, Smith Barney sold 300 December and 100 August while Refco Inc bought 100 each August and September and 200 December, traders said.
In soyoil, commercials were light sellers. ADM sold 300 October and 100 December, Produce Grain sold 300 December and 100 March and Central Soya sold 100 December.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 22,000 lots, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 22,596. Soyoil volume was pegged at 20,000 lots, against Tuesday's 24,354.
